item.title: From physics-informed machine learning to de-Occamising physics: the case of the currentmagnetisation hypothesis
item.description: Occam’s razor implies that a fundamental theory should describe diverse systems with few adjustable parameters. We test how far the current–magnetisation hypothesis (CMH), a microscopic description of the Orsted magnetic induction, must be enlarged to cover wires, dilute plasmas and molecules. That is, we attempt a de-Occamisation of CMH. After finding failures in the original formulation, two repairs define the new formulation, CMH-ML: an adaptive k rule removes density-dependent plasma suppression, and a curl of correlation potentials removes the divergent-energy 1/r field around bounded currents. The Cu-wire-refitted baseline, L0, gives a Biot–Savart-like dilute-plasma response but severely underestimates benzene NMR shifts. A three-scalar iteration, L1, misses the joint wire–NMR target; a learned-interior iteration, L2, and a nine-parameter reduced refit, L3, reach it. L0–L3 remain within a few percent of the Biot–Savart dilute-plasma response. Their graphene-nanoribbon fields differ strongly: L3 overshoots the near-ribbon benchmark, so L2 is retained provisionally for the final predictions. The wire and benzene fits and the dilute-plasma response therefore cannot separate L2 from L3; the near-ribbon field can, and so it is where the flexibility CMH requires remains to be settled.

item.title: Benchmarking Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials for Reactive Chemistry: Failure Modes in Nitromethane Decomposition
item.description: The failure modes of ab initio methods and empirical force fields are well documented, but those of machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) in reactive chemistry remain largely uncharacterized. We benchmark five MLIPs on condensed-phase nitromethane decomposition against coupled-cluster dissociation energies and published simulations, and trace each model’s failure to a specific component: the global spin label of MACE-OMol-0 and UMA-S-1P1 produces a spurious ~25 kcal/mol rise as fragments separate, gaps in the training data of ANI-1xnr cause it to underbind dissociation into two polyatomic radicals by up to 48 kcal/mol, and the absence of close-contact configurations from the training data of MACE-OFF23 and MACEOsaka24 leads to unphysical energies at short interatomic distances, more severely in MACEOFF23. The responsible component determines the remedy: the spin-label artifact cannot be fixed within the models’ input format, the ANI-1xnr error is corrected to within 1 kcal/mol by physics-constrained data augmentation, and the short-range failure of MACE-OFF23 persists even with a standard screened nuclear repulsion term. Because corrected dissociation energies do not by themselves restore physical decomposition kinetics, we join recent calls to judge MLIPs by their failure modes and predicted observables rather than by aggregate energy and force errors.

item.title: Multitask Neural Networks for Multi-Solvent Solubility Prediction: Joint Learning with Lipophilicity, Melting Point, and Hydration Free Energy
item.description: The accurate prediction of solute solubility (LogS) and related properties such as partition coefficient (LogP), melting point (MP), and hydration free energy (∆Ghyd) plays a vital role in molecular design and specifically drug discovery. Data-driven machine learning approaches have received considerable attention due to their ability to provide fast and accurate predictions. However, the scarcity of high-quality datasets poses a significant obstacle to their wide applications. One strategy to circumvent this challenge is to employ multitask (MT) models which allow sharing of information and exploitation of correlations across various tasks, thereby addressing the limitations in data for specific tasks. In this work, two MT algorithms based on neural networks and the multi-explanation graph attention network (MEGAN) were developed and used for the simultaneous prediction of 19 tasks comprising 16 datasets of LogS together with one dataset of each of LogP, MP, and ∆Ghyd as helping tasks. In addition, single-task (ST) versions of the aforementioned models together with four more models, namely graph attention networks, random forest regression, Gaussian process regression, and support vector regression were analyzed for comparative purposes. It was found that both MT-DNN and MT-MEGAN models trained on all 19 tasks on average outperform all the other models when comparing the mean R2 values, with MT-DNN additionally achieving the lowest weighted RMSE and enabling predictive performance even for datasets with fewer than 50 data points. However, for the individual tasks there was no consistent improvement of the MT models.

item.title: Explainable Machine Learning for Low-Emission Methane Tri-Reforming: Carbon Formation, Hydrogen Production, and Operating-Window Optimization
item.description: Tri-reforming of methane (TRM) is a promising route for producing hydrogen-rich syngas while partially utilizing CO2, but its deployment is limited by trade-offs among methane conversion, syngas composition, reactor duty, and carbon deposition. In this study, a Gibbsequilibrium model in Aspen Plus was used to generate a database of 46,464 operating points spanning temperature, pressure, and inlet H2O/CH4, CO2/CH4, and O2/CH4 ratios. Decision tree, random forest, XGBoost, and artificial neural network models were trained and compared, followed by SHAP and permutation-importance analysis and multi-objective genetic-algorithm optimization. The neural network showed the best predictive performance. Explainability analysis identified temperature as the dominant factor governing carbon formation, followed by steam, carbon dioxide, and oxygen feed ratios. Optimization revealed multiple distinct operating windows, confirming that no single universal optimum exists and demonstrating a rapid, interpretable framework for low-emission TRM screening and design.

item.title: Molecular dynamics and docking study of an illustrative VHH-like model at MICA α3 and small-molecule ENPP1 and EZH2 ligands
item.description: Some tumours evade natural killer (NK) cells by proteolytically cleaving the stress ligands MICA and MICB near the cell membrane within their α3 domains. Here I evaluated an illustrative, computationally constructed VHH-like model, VHH1, in complex with the isolated human MICA α3 domain (UniProt residues 182 to 274) using structure prediction, explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (MD), and implicit-solvent rescoring, alongside small-molecule docking against two additional tumour immune-evasion targets, ENPP1 and EZH2. Across The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) cohorts in UALCAN (8,609 primary tumours and 738 unpaired normal tissue samples across 24 cohorts), median MICA transcript levels in tumours exceeded normal tissue medians in 13 of 24 cohorts overall, and in 9 of the 17 cohorts with more than five normal samples, while normal tissues also carried substantial baseline MICA RNA (medians 2.40 to 5.07 log2[TPM + 1]), indicating that bulk transcript levels alone do not establish tumour specificity. Sequence alignment confirmed that the human MICA and MICB α3 domains share 87 of 93 residues (93.5% identity), but MICB binding was not tested by docking or MD. AlphaFold 3 folded the individual VHH1 and MICA α3 domains with high confidence (chain pTM 0.87 and 0.85 to 0.86; n = 5 samples from seed 250104442), but the predicted complex had moderate global confidence (pTM 0.57 to 0.60) and low interface confidence (ipTM 0.13 to 0.22). Across three independent 100 ns MD simulations (2,001 frames per replicate), VHH1 remained internally folded (whole-run internal Cα RMSD 1.11 to 1.55 Å; domain-fitted Cα RMSF 0.67 to 0.72 Å) and retained contacts with the isolated MICA α3 domain in three distinct binding orientations. Replicates 1 and 3 maintained contact with four MICA α3 anchor residues (Ser193, Thr198, Gln228, and Arg247), whereas Replicate 2 shifted onto a lateral stalk surface involving framework region 3 residues; persistence in a pre-assembled complex does not prove binding affinity or shedding inhibition. Comparative single-trajectory OpenMM MM/GBSA estimates across 33 time-correlated frames per replicate (20 to 100 ns) were −49.1 ± 14.0, −20.2 ± 10.9, and −30.6 ± 5.0 kcal/mol for Replicates 1, 2, and 3, respectively. In AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 (n = 3 seeds per ligand), redocking the co-crystallised ligand TZV into human ENPP1 (PDB 6WEW) passed validation (top-pose RMSD 0.67 to 0.91 Å; best score −9.95 kcal/mol), although neither TZV nor the proposed model compounds Compound 1 (−9.10 kcal/mol) and Compound 2 (−10.32 kcal/mol) achieved inner-sphere Zn2+ coordination. Redocking S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH) into human EZH2 (PDB 5HYN, chains A and D) failed validation (top-pose RMSD 7.78 to 7.86 Å) because Vina scored the crystal pose (−5.57 kcal/mol as-is; −7.05 kcal/mol after local minimisation) worse than alternative poses (−8.24 kcal/mol), rendering the tazemetostat docking result (−8.94 kcal/mol) strictly exploratory. All findings are unvalidated computational predictions that require experimental testing.

item.title: Mechanosensitive ion transport in hexagonal boron nitride nanopores
item.description: In biological systems, mechanical strain can trigger strong changes in ion conductance and signaling, yet in synthetic nanopores, achieving similar mechanosensitive behavior has been a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that subtle mechanical strain can induce strong modulation of ionic current in small hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) nanopores. Using hydrostatic pressure to apply small lateral strain to free-standing single-layer h-BN membranes featuring triangular sub-1-nm nanopores, we observed ion conductance modulation exceeding 1 30% under 0.5% strain. We attribute this response to the strain-dependent interplay of ionpore and ion-water interactions within the nanopore. The measured mechanosensitivity values also agreed strongly with those obtained from modeling of strain-tunable transport in ensembles of h-BN nanopores. These findings establish a framework for developing strain-responsive membranes for applications in molecular separations and sensing.

item.title: A generative neural network architecture for structure elucidation
item.description: IMPORTANT REMARK: We found an error in our code. The numbers and potentially the conclusions cannot be relied on in this and the previous version. We are working on rectifying this.Determining molecular structure is central to chemistry. One-dimensional (1D) 1H and 13C nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a standard technique in small molecule structure determination, but deducing a structure from these spectra remains challenging because of the vast chemical space involved. Deep learning models that predict structures directly from NMR data have shown potential in navigating this space, but are trained largely on simulated spectra and perform poorly on real experimental data. Here we present a transformer model trained purely on experimental NMR data from approximately 1 million molecules, which takes 1D 1H and 13C NMR peak lists together with molecular weight (readily obtained from mass spectrometry) and generates candidate structures as SMILES strings. On a held-out test set, our model identified the correct structure among 15 candidates for 56.6% of molecules with up to 19 heavy atoms (34.8% overall). On a benchmark of 86 experimental spectra, it was more than four times as accurate as the published NMR2Struct model at every candidate pool size, while generating more chemically valid candidates. Even when the exact structure was missed, its best candidates remained structurally close to the target, and its incorrect candidates retained many of the target’s functional groups, making them useful starting points for structure elucidation. These results demonstrate that training on experimental spectra substantially improves structure prediction from routine 1D NMR data.

item.title: Motion in Stillness: An Open-Source Python Toolkit for Visualizing Time-Dependent Hydrogen Wavefunctions
item.description: Orbital shapes and nodes are core learning objectives in chemistry and physics. Many tools can render a wavefunc- tion’s phase as a color map. Yet rendering it is not teaching it: students often cannot explain what phase means, nor where Ψ’s time dependence lies. Since the density |Ψ|2 of a stationary state is constant, many infer Ψ is static. The opposite is true. For a complex stationary state Ψ(t) = ψe−iEnt/ℏ, the phase argΨ = argψ −Ent/ℏ is time-dependent, advancing uniformly everywhere except at the nodes; because all points advance in step, phase differences remain fixed, and the nodal structure is unchanged. At a node (ψ = 0) the amplitude vanishes and the phase is undefined, changing abruptly across the nodal surface. Ψ’s time dependence thus resides in its phase, sharply distinguished at nodal and non-nodal points. We present Time-HWV, an open-source Python toolkit that decouples and animates the real part, imaginary part, and density in synchronized 2D cross-section and 3D views. Students observe the quadrature oscillation of Re[Ψ(t)] and Im[Ψ(t)] while confirming that |Ψ(t)|2 = |ψ|2 is invariant. Time-HWV offers 2D cross-sections (slices), 3D surface plots of those cross-sections (height fields), and interactive Plotly volume renderings in a lightweight NumPy/SciPy/Matplotlib package, with standalone executables requiring no programming environment. Code and manual are included as Supporting Information.

item.title: ILMlip: fast and universal machine-learning interatomic potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.33538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale pretrained machine-learned interatomic potentials keep growing more accurate as new models appear at a rapid pace, and more expensive: the current leader of Matbench Discovery as of November 2026 (F1 score 0.935) has $9.9\times10^7$ parameters and took 3.6 thousand GPU-hours to train. The ILMlip potentials presented here are optimised for speed as well as zero-shot accuracy. They are equivariant, conservative message-passing potentials in which every component is arranged for throughput: little work per pair of atoms and as much as needed per atom. Through ASE on one GPU, they run molecular dynamics up to about $10^3$ times faster than state-of-the-art message-passing potentials such as MACE (medium) and up to five times faster than NEP89 and DPA-4.1C. At the same time, six sizes with $1.4\times10^5$ to $2.8\times10^7$ parameters, pretrained on materials, molecules and solid acids, reach F1 scores of 0.75 to 0.91 on Matbench Discovery, placing the largest within 0.03 of the current leader. They therefore suit high-throughput, large or long simulations, and, being transferable, they are strong starting points for fine-tuning. Fine-tuned to six materials, the model of size S comes close to the ab initio force errors of a fine-tuned MACE, so it reaches reference-level accuracy at about 50 ns per atom and step (Cu fcc). Their components can be adopted separately, as a starting point for architectures with even better ratios of speed to accuracy. The ILMlip implementation is available at https://github.com/jhaens/ilmlip

item.title: Phono3GPU: GPU-Accelerated Linear Tetrahedron Integration for Phonon Thermal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.33912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Materials with high or low thermal conductivity are increasingly important for thermal management and energy technologies. Machine-learned interatomic potentials have accelerated anharmonic force-constant calculations, shifting the bottleneck toward phonon transport calculations for large materials datasets. Existing GPU solvers often rely on smearing, whose width can require material-dependent choices, while the linear tetrahedron method used in phono3py avoids this parameter but becomes costly for complex structures. Here we introduce Phono3GPU, which reformulates three-phonon scattering and linear tetrahedron integration for massively parallel GPU execution. Across benchmark crystals, Phono3GPU accelerates total calculations by up to 41 times relative to a CPU implementation, with larger gains for complex unit cells, and by 2 to 6 times relative to a recent GPU plug-in for phono3py. We further demonstrate atom-resolved scattering analysis in defective silicon supercells as an application enabled by the reduced computational cost. Phono3GPU thus lowers the cost of tetrahedron-based thermal-conductivity calculations and of detailed investigations of structure-dependent phonon transport.

item.title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.33913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing surface-capping ligands for high-performance halide perovskite nanocrystals requires navigating a vast molecular space while discovering design rules that govern ligand-surface interactions. Here, we introduce PerovAgent, an autonomous multi-agent framework that combines large language model (LLM)-driven scientific reasoning with computational tools for atomistic model construction, machine-learned interatomic potential evaluation, and statistical validation. Across ten independent campaigns on CsPbBr3 surfaces, PerovAgent adaptively explored and refined diverse ligand chemistries while progressively improving the binding-energy objective. Beyond optimization, the framework converts recurring chemical observations into explicit design principles that can be statistically evaluated. Of 35 formulated principles, 19 were prospectively supported, of which seven also passed the confound audit, highlighting the need to systematically validate plausible LLM-generated hypotheses during autonomous discovery. A recurrent alkynyl-phosphonate principle was further examined using density functional theory, which reproduced the predicted energetic preference. These results demonstrate an autonomous discovery framework that not only searches molecular space and optimizes the scalar objective but also transforms its search trajectory into systematically testable design principles. The framework can also be extended to more complex ligands, including zwitterionic, multidentate, and polymerizable ligands, to explore a wider range of ligand-surface interactions and uncover new design principles for halide perovskite nanocrystals.

item.title: Exploring Physical Mechanisms Underlying the Emergence of Collective Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.33988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emergence of collective order from disordered constituents is a hallmark of active matter, and the Vicsek model (VM) serves as a paradigmatic system for its study. However, whether density-induced emergence in the VM differs between angular (intrinsic) and vectorial (extrinsic) noise, and what mechanisms govern the transitions, remain largely unexplored. Remarkably, we uncover that collective order emerges from a disordered state in a continuous-like manner under intrinsic noise but abruptly under extrinsic noise. Combining nonequilibrium landscape-flux theory with a coarse-grained mapping method, we show that the landscape evolves continuously from a single basin to two and back to one under intrinsic noise, but the two-basin landscape appears abruptly under extrinsic noise across the critical transition to flocking. The counterclockwise nonequilibrium flux sustains global circular motion, providing the driving force for reshaping the landscape. The mean flux and entropy production rate change steeply near the emergence threshold and exhibit pronounced peaks within the coexistence region, identifying them as the dynamical and thermodynamic origins of emergence. Our findings reveal a distinct abrupt emergence under extrinsic noise and offer deeper mechanistic insight, practical applications (e.g., locating phase boundaries and distinguishing transition types), and extensibility to other nonequilibrium collective systems.

item.title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
item.description: arXiv:2611.34156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials transfer well across chemical and structural space, yet their reliability for highly disordered metallic states is less established. Metallic glasses are a demanding benchmark: they have traditionally been modeled with Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potentials fitted to specific compositions, while ab initio molecular dynamics remains too expensive at the required sizes and timescales. Using the prototypical Cu-Zr-Al glass, we show that foundation potentials capture structural disorder, reproducing the structure, quenching dynamics, and elastic, mechanical and thermal properties of the amorphous state at near first-principles accuracy. We benchmark MACE foundation models against a classical EAM potential along molecular dynamics quenches, validating against density functional theory and experiment, first at Cu46Zr46Al8 and then across the good glass-forming region of the ternary. We further test two specialization routes: fine-tuning on glass structures generated with Lennard-Jones surrogate models, and on automatically generated small periodic cells (ASSYST). Models pre-trained on databases that include non-equilibrium liquid and amorphous configurations, such as OMAT, are accurate and transferable across composition out of the box, clearly outperforming the composition-specific EAM potential. Fine-tuning on target glass structures brings only modest gains, while specialization on small crystalline cells degrades the description of disorder. The readiness of foundation potentials for disordered metals is therefore set mainly by the diversity of their pre-training data rather than by system-specific fine-tuning, shifting the modeling effort from bespoke dataset generation to pre-training coverage and careful validation of the resulting dynamics.

item.title: Patterns and correlations in time-reversal symmetry breaking
item.description: arXiv:2611.34244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking is the hallmark of non-equilibrium statistical physics. This notwithstanding, in translationally invariant systems, it is almost always treated only as a global quantity. We propose to use the local entropy production rate as a spatio-temporal field to describe extended homogeneous non-equilibrium systems. We find that this field generically displays spatial correlations, with a typical length that grows as we approach some non-equilibrium phase transitions. We also show that the correlation length associated with the local entropy production rate follows heretofore unknown scaling laws involving control parameters as well as the observation time used for trajectories. Our work paves the way to the use of the local entropy production as a powerful observable to identify the scale and source of TRS breaking in non-equilibrium systems.

item.title: Intrinsically nonlinear nanomechanical resonator toward the single-phonon Kerr regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.34345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Manipulating a physical system at the single-quantum level typically requires an anharmonic energy spectrum. Nanomechanical resonators, however, are commonly admitted to be linear objects in the single-phonon regime, thus motivating most efforts to employ external sources of nonlinearity at the cost of added relaxation and decoherence channels. Here, we take a radically different approach by directly exploiting strong intrinsic mechanical nonlinearities. We quantify this nonlinearity using a novel method based on the coupling between bending modes. Using this technique, we establish an upper bound of 34.0 +/- 9.7 phonons for the onset of intrinsically mechanical bistability. In addition, we highlight a new tuning mechanism based on a mechanical polarization angle of an upward-buckled nanotube resonator allowing us to reach an optimal working point. Extrapolating this level of intrinsic nonlinearity to realistically shorter resonators shows that the single-phonon Kerr regime is within reach, allowing for the realization of purely mechanical Schr\"odinger-cat states and highly coherent mechanical qubits.

item.title: EGQCA Code: automated high-throughput thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.34551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modeling disordered systems from first principles across the full composition range is a long-standing computational challenge. We present a code package implementing the extended generalized quasichemical approximation (EGQCA), which describes solid solutions through the statistics of a finite set of clusters and enables their thermodynamic modeling at arbitrary compositions and temperatures. The package automates the complete workflow and interfaces with both DFT codes and universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs). We show that replacing DFT with uMLIPs reduces the cost of the cluster calculations by up to five orders of magnitude while preserving the thermodynamic predictions. To make computationally demanding properties tractable, we additionally introduce a cluster-selection algorithm that identifies the most relevant configurations. Together, these developments establish EGQCA as a fast and accurate framework for the thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions and a practical route toward high-throughput screening of disordered materials.

item.title: Frozen Phonons on Dense $\mathbf{q}$-Grids Using Set Covers
item.description: arXiv:2611.34638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phonon dynamics determine a vast number of properties in the solid state, such as the heat capacity, thermal expansion, and thermal conductivity. Phonons are obtained through the dynamical matrix, which, in the frozen phonon approach, is calculated as a finite difference derivative of the analytical Hellmann-Feynman force. This approach unfortunately typically suffers from requiring very large supercells, even for modest $\mathbf{q}$-grids. The non-diagonal supercell method remedies this issue by determining the smallest supercell commensurate with a given $\mathbf{q}$-point, drastically reducing the supercell size, but in turn requiring a new supercell for each $\mathbf{q}$-point on the grid. This introduces redundancy, however, since a single non-diagonal supercell may be commensurate with several $\mathbf{q}$-points. In this work I present a method to determine a minimal set of supercells, such that every $\mathbf{q}$-point on the grid is commensurate with at least one supercell. I present an algorithm to solve the problem and prove that it yields the optimal solution, before summarizing the algorithm using pseudocode. The scaling of the number of supercells with the density of the grid is discussed. Numerical results on a variety of systems show the significant computational advantage of the method, which increases with the density of the grid.

item.title: Verified experience improves materials prediction with large language models
item.description: arXiv:2611.33195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. We present MatRecall, a framework that lets large language models store verified predictions, with evidence, outcome and error, as episodes and recall them without retraining. MatRecall improved median performance by 62% over a memory-free model, exceeded specialized models on 11 tasks, remained useful after feedback stopped and transferred between related tasks. Verified experience could become a reusable resource for self-improving discovery loops.

item.title: Geometry Sets the Neutral MLIP-DFT Gap in Non-Covalent Binding, and Charged Systems Fail
item.description: arXiv:2611.33830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are widely expected to substitute for explicit quantum chemistry when screening molecular interactions. On non-covalent binding we find that this expectation holds for neutral chemistry and fails for charged chemistry. We audit the FAIRChem UMA OMol head, without task-specific fine-tuning, on 5,567 probe-target dimers from 18 benchmarks across nine fidelity arms, using RAPIDS (Rapid Atomistic Probe-target Interaction Discovery Scaffold), a training-free inference-time scaffold. First, on neutral chemistry RAPIDS reaches a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.37 kcal/mol, matching or beating every explicit DFT single-point fidelity (1.42-1.50 kcal/mol), so the remaining MLIP-DFT gap is geometric rather than a learned-surface error. Second, charged systems form a qualitatively different regime: MAE jumps to 8.5-22.9 kcal/mol across three charged benchmarks; DFT single-point rescoring does not restore accuracy, geometry reoptimization restores it for ionic hydrogen bonds and ion-molecule dimers, and the failure persists across all three MLIP backbones. Third, the residual failures are structured: signed biases cluster by chemistry family, and whether a fidelity fails catastrophically transfers across families more reliably than error magnitude, enabling cost-aware fidelity selection. RAPIDS-Select, a closed-form rule on cheap precomputed features, uses about 37% less compute than a strong static DFT baseline at matched accuracy, and on a newly computed charged benchmark cuts the catastrophe rate from 68% to 5.7%. On WetSenseBench, a wet-lab-grounded host-guest selectivity benchmark from eight sensing studies, RAPIDS without DFT follow-up recovers 82.9% pair-level agreement on the seven studies above its ~1 kcal/mol precision floor.

item.title: SCO-Hyper-Meta-Double-GroupNN: A Double-Group SU(2) Hyper-/Meta-Graph Neural Network for Cooperative Spin-Crossover Potential Energy Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.34547v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning potential energy surfaces for magnetic materials requires resolving coupled local spin manifolds and geometric frustration. We introduce SCO-Hyper-Meta-Double-GroupNN, a geometry-only architecture combining a pretrained O(3)-equivariant backbone with SU(2) spinor Hamiltonians and cooperative hyper-/meta-graph interactions. Analytic thermal spinor density matrices provide non-polynomial two- and three-body structural invariants, while frustrated-triangle hyperedges and a multi-shell sideway gate couple geometric representations to local spin manifolds. A variationally consistent, doubly-centered zero-gauge free-energy functional couples multiplet occupations and signed spin orientations, yielding conservative autograd forces without spin inputs at inference. On a first-principles Co-Cr-Ni benchmark comprising 346 training and 59 held-out validation supercells across crystalline, amorphous, glassy, and liquid regimes, compact models with 56k-77k parameters outperform a 207k-parameter spin-conditioned magnetic MACE baseline. Energy MAE decreases by 37-44%, reaching 3.82 versus 6.83 meV/atom, and force MAE decreases by 10.8-14.2 meV/Angstrom, reaching 165.8-169.2 versus 180.0 meV/Angstrom. The models preserve Kramers degeneracy to within $6\times10^{-15}$ eV, predict equilibrium local magnetic moments from geometry alone with an absolute-moment MAE of $0.181\,\mu_B$, and support stable molecular dynamics up to 2,200 K. This framework integrates local spinor symmetry and cooperative magnetic interactions into geometry-only interatomic potentials.

item.title: Information-Theoretic Diagnostics of Collective Modes and Vortex Dynamics in Rotating Two-Dimensional Bose-Einstein Condensates
item.description: arXiv:2604.24557v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of a two-dimensional rotating Bose gas confined in a symmetric anharmonic trap, employing the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method for bosons (MCTDHB). We study states ranging from vortex-free configurations to multicharged (giant) vortices, prepared by tuning the rotation frequency, and analyze their response to sudden interaction and trap quenches. In vortex-free states, interaction quenches induce regular breathing-like dynamics, whereas in the presence of giant vortices they lead to symmetry-breaking surface excitations. In contrast, trap deformations that excite quadrupole-like modes produce stable oscillations in vortex-free condensates but trigger rapid, irregular, and effectively chaotic multimode dynamics in multicharged vortices. To characterize these processes beyond conventional density and phase observables, we employ information-theoretic (IT) measures, including marginal and joint spatial entropies, mutual information, and Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence, supplemented by an angular-resolved KL measure that quantifies azimuthal density redistribution and symmetry breaking. We find that chaotic splitting is accompanied by a pronounced growth of information-theoretic indicators, signaling the buildup of many-body correlations and increasing complexity in the system dynamics. Our results demonstrate the extreme sensitivity of giant vortices to excitation protocols and establish IT measures as quantitative global diagnostics that complement conventional observables by characterizing spatial redistribution and correlations during complex vortex dynamics.

item.title: Anisotropic Crystallization Kinetics and Interfacial Dynamics of Phase-Change Material Sb$_2$S$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2605.20785v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Antimony sulfide (Sb$_2$S$_3$), an Earth-abundant and sustainable chalcogenide, has emerged as a promising phase change material (PCM) due to its ultra-low optical losses, broadband transparency, and reversible phase-change capacity. In this work, we developed a machine learning force field based on the moment tensor potential approach, allowing us to understand the atomistic origin of the structural evolution and crystallization kinetics in Sb$_2$S$_3$ for the first time, by enabling large-scale molecular dynamics simulations (up to 7680 atoms for 40 ns). Sb$_2$S$_3$ has anisotropic growth rates with the (100) facet ($Pnma$ space group) exhibiting the fastest growth due to the strong Sb-S covalent bonding along its quasi-1D ribbon-like structure of its crystalline phase. The maximum growth rate was observed at 875 K, with an optimal undercooling degree of ~100 K, significantly lower than other PCMs like Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ (GST) and GeTe. The activation energy for crystal growth was calculated be around 0.56 eV. Interfacial atomic dynamics revealed an Arrhenius-to-non-Arrhenius transition at ~800 K, with the (100) facet showing the highest diffusion activation energy of 1.56 eV. Unlike the GST and GeTe, the lower activation energy for crystal growth in Sb$_2$S$_3$ indicates that its heterogeneous crystallization is interface-controlled rather than diffusion-limited, with atomic attachment at the solid-liquid interface being energetically favoured over long-range atomic transport. Bonding and ring statistics analyses confirmed that directional covalent bonding plays a fundamental role in guiding structural ordering during crystal growth. These findings provide key insights into the structural, thermodynamic, and kinetic properties of Sb$_2$S$_3$, paving the way for optimizing its functionality including switching speed, reliability, and energy efficiency.

item.title: Symmetry-protected cubic-touching topological surface bands with tunable singularities
item.description: arXiv:2607.19265v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a class of topological surface bands in three-dimensional topological insulators that have symmetry-protected cubic-order band touching. Within the symmetry constraint, the band dispersion can continuously vary between cubic dispersion, moat band and multi-mini-valley structure with van Hove singularities by adjusting particle-hole asymmetry and anisotropy. Thus, there is a family of tunable density-of-state singularities ranging from power-law to logarithmic divergences. This offrs a versatile platform for engineering strongly correlated phases of matter in topological surface states. We provide an example realization in a prism-lattice tight-binding model of angular-momentum-3/2 electrons.

item.title: Systematic and accurate anharmonic formation free energies of metastable defects via a constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force framework
item.description: arXiv:2608.20902v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Computing the formation free energies of metastable defects at finite temperature remains challenging due to anharmonicity, the multiplicity of basins and the frequent occurrence of migration events. Using the previously introduced constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force method (BABFc) [1], we establish a practical framework for computing restricted anharmonic formation free energies associated with individual metastable defect basins. We demonstrate that BABFc can be exploited as a robust, systematic and numerically efficient tool for addressing a long standing bottleneck in atomistic materials science: the finite temperature thermodynamic characterization of metastable defects in complex, highly anharmonic energy landscapes. The proposed workflow requires only a reference local minimum and a confinement strategy and does not rely on defect specific collective variables. It therefore provides a general route to assign well-defined free energies to individual metastable basins, even when these basins are separated by low barriers. In this setting, BABFc enables stable, bias corrected free energy estimates with statistical accuracies at the meV/atom level and a very low failure rate, including for systems containing approximately one thousand atoms. We demonstrate this capability through thousands of independent free energy calculations covering hundreds of four-interstitial and four-vacancy configurations in bcc {\alpha}-Fe over a broad temperature range, using both a traditional empirical potential and a data driven force field. The study also highlights the critical role of energy landscape regularity in defect thermodynamics. This approach has many powerful applications, ranging from building extensive databases of free energies for data-driven force fields to enabling fully automated workflows for characterizing defects in materials at finite temperatures.

item.title: The role of entropy production and thermodynamic uncertainty relations in the asymmetric thermalization of open quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2510.05072v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The asymmetry between heating and cooling in open quantum systems is a hallmark of nonequilibrium dynamics. Here, we investigate the thermalization of a quantum system weakly coupled to a bosonic thermal bath under detailed balance, focusing on the entropy production rate and the quantum thermokinetic uncertainty relation (TKUR). Within the sector of states that remain diagonal in the energy basis we derive a perturbative expression for the time-dependent entropy production rate by expanding the relative entropy around equilibrium in terms of Liouvillian eigenmodes. Through this expansion, we determine that the spectral gap, the overlap of the initial state with the slowest decay mode, and the mode weight control the entropy production. Particularly for the thermal qubit, the ratio of the initial rates of heating and cooling has an exact closed form. Heating involves a higher initial entropy production, and hence faster thermalization, solely because of its larger spectral gap, i.e., the bath-temperature dependence of the dissipative rate. The TKUR is then used as a diagnostic tool that relates the asymmetry to the precision bounds on heat-current fluctuations. The analysis presented here is intended to clarify the thermodynamic origin of the asymmetry within the well-controlled Markovian case.

item.title: Scalable Low-Cost Laboratory Automation: A Digital Twin-Integrated Robotic Platform for Autonomous Liquid Handling (RAINBOT)
item.description: arXiv:2607.20662v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Laboratory automation accelerates discovery, yet its adoption is constrained by the high cost, proprietary design, and limited remote supervisability of commercial liquid-handling systems. This work presents RAINBOT\textsuperscript{TM}, a low-cost, openly reproducible liquid-handling robot built by converting a consumer-grade Cartesian 3D printer (Elegoo Neptune 4 Max). The printer extruder is replaced by a precision single-channel pipette actuated through the printer's own G-code-driven X--Y--Z gantry, with plunger and tip-eject motions effected by two compact linear actuators under Python control. To make experiments transparent and remotely supervisable, a browser-based digital twin is implemented to synchronise bidirectionally with the physical platform, mirroring kinematics and pipetting states in real time and exposing remote monitoring, intervention, and an emergency stop from any web browser. As a proof of concept, RAINBOT\textsuperscript{TM} performed sequential exchanges of differently coloured aqueous solutions while an integrated colour sensor quantified the resulting mixtures; measured red, yellow, and blue (RYB) responses agreed with expected mixing behaviour to within a mean absolute error of two percentage points, validating correct execution and real-time tracking. Closing the loop, the platform is coupled to the CEID\textsuperscript{TM} (Cooperative Explorer for Inverse Design) framework, which recasts experimentation from iterative manual guessing into a goal-directed inverse-design search while keeping a human in the loop. The complete hardware costs under US\$1300, which is roughly an order of magnitude below entry-level commercial handlers, thereby establishing an accessible physical--virtual framework for self-driving laboratory automation.

item.title: CompMat-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Computational Materials Science
item.description: arXiv:2610.00636v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Evaluating AI agents on scientific research tasks is constrained by the time and resources required for the underlying experiments or calculations. In computational materials research, repeating the same expensive simulations across agents and trials can make evaluation impractical. We introduce CompMat-Bench, a benchmark of 94 tasks derived from recently published computational materials studies, each asking agents to complete a step toward achieving the study's scientific goal. We reproduce the research steps in advance and assess agents on preparing inputs and analyzing outputs for expensive simulations, so expensive simulations can be avoided during evaluation. The reproduced inputs and results serve as ground truth for grading agents with fixed rules, without an LLM judge. We extend the benchmark to four evaluation conditions: single tasks and workflows composed of related tasks, each with full or reduced methodological guidance. In a workflow, the agent runs all simulations itself. With full guidance on single tasks, agents based on nine LLMs demonstrate the ability to complete individual materials research steps, with pass rates of 62.8-97.9% across 94 tasks. Both longer workflows and reduced guidance can limit agent performance, but in different ways for different agents: they lower the pass rates of the weaker agents, whereas the stronger agents fall only when a long workflow is combined with reduced guidance. Failure analysis attributes more failures to scientific errors than to errors in software usage. CompMat-Bench provides a basis for comparing agents on the steps of real materials research and for analyzing agent failure modes.

item.title: Patterning Capture Oligonucleotides on DUV-Defined Silicon Sites: Toward Sequence-Programmable DNA Origami Placement
item.description: Combining top-down lithography with DNA self-assembly could place molecularly defined structures at chosen positions in semiconductor devices. Placement of DNA origami on lithographic patterns currently relies on Mg2+-mediated adsorption, which is sensitive to ionic conditions and cannot distinguish origami by sequence. As a step toward sequence-programmable placement, we pattern capture oligonucleotides on silicon sites defined by deep-ultraviolet (DUV) photolithography. Silanizing through the developed photoresist, and removing the resist before the oligonucleotide is applied, confines the functional layer to the sites. Amine-terminated, Cy5-labelled strands were retained on the sites with three coupling chemistries: epoxide (GPTMS), EDC/NHS-activated carboxyl (CTES) and aldehyde (APTES with glutaraldehyde). In preliminary deposition experiments on GPTMS-functionalized chips, incubation with 1 nM square origami tiles carrying complementary extensions left features 40–60 nm across on the functionalized regions and none detectable on the surrounding oxide by SEM. These features were absent from a chip carrying capture strands only, and by AFM the sites of the tile-incubated chip were 0.8–1.4 nm higher and about three times rougher than those of the capture-strand-only chip. The features were also absent from the sites of a chip incubated with 10 nM tiles, their shape was not resolved, and triangle-based pentagonal and hexagonal assemblies were not found on the sites. Whether attachment depends on the capture sequence has not yet been tested. We set out the controls, surface passivation and imaging needed to establish hybridization-directed placement of single origami on DUV-defined sites.

item.title: Bayesian Optimization for Constructing Quantum Control Fields in Optically-Excited Heterostructure Nanomaterials
item.description: We present a high-dimensional machine learning framework based on Bayesian optimization (BO) for constructing optimal control fields to drive targeted quantum-state transitions in nanoscale heterostructures. To address the large dimensionality of these time-domain quantum control fields, we introduce a gradientinformed directional subspace optimization (DSO) strategy that adaptively projects the problem into low-dimensional subspaces defined by gradient-derived directions. Within this framework, both standard BO and sparse axis-aligned subspace BO (SAASBO) are employed using Gaussian process surrogates with gradient information and Expected Improvement acquisition functions. Compared to traditional gradientbased line search methods, the BO-DSO and SAASBO-DSO techniques demonstrate faster convergence, improved sample efficiency, and more physically realistic control fields with reduced oscillatory behavior. Overall, this work demonstrates that combining Bayesian optimization with gradient-informed subspace expansion provides an effective and scalable solution to high-dimensional quantum optimal control problems in realistic quantum materials and devices.

item.title: A machine-readable specification of the ISOS stability protocols, with protocol classification and refusing degradation metrics for perovskite photovoltaics
item.description: The ISOS consensus protocols define how accelerated stability tests on perovskite and organic photovoltaic devices should be run and reported, but they exist as prose and tables rather than as anything a machine can check. Two failures follow. Reported test conditions frequently do not determine a protocol designation, and the gap is usually one or two specific conditions that were never stated. Separately, the lifetime figure T80 denotes at least three distinct quantities, differing in which performance value is taken as the reference and when the clock starts, and published values are rarely qualified by which was used. We present isoskit, an open Python package that encodes 33 ISOS protocols as a versioned machine-readable specification with a JSON Schema, classifies a reported measurement into its protocol designation or names the conditions preventing designation, and extracts lifetime figures of merit under explicitly named reference conventions, returning a structured refusal wherever the reported measurement does not support extraction. Using the encoded specification we report three computational results. First, round-trip validation shows that 27 of 33 protocols are uniquely identifiable from their tabulated stress conditions; the remaining six form three degenerate pairs whose distinction lies in equipment and cycle profile rather than in stress conditions, one of which is induced by the encoding of inert-atmosphere humidity. Second, an exhaustive ablation over all 270,336 combinations of withheld conditions identifies six conditions without which no protocol in the set can be designated, and shows that withholding a single condition reduces the designated fraction from 81.8 % to 25.9 %. Third, on a two-phase ageing model the reference conventions diverge by a factor of 10.4 at a burn-in depth of 25 %, while linear interpolation of the crossing time remains accurate to 2 h at a 400 h measurement interval for which the defensible bracketing uncertainty is 400 h. The package is MIT licensed, has no runtime dependencies, and generates its own reference documentation from the specification.
