item.title: Evaluating cofolding methods for protein–macrocycle structure prediction
item.description: The accuracy of general-purpose cofolding models in predicting binding poses for novel protein–macrocycle complexes with little experimental structural precedent remains poorly characterized. We developed MacroCycle-Benchmark, which links chemically verified ligand structures to their experimental binding poses and protein environments across 1,861 cases. We evaluated six general-purpose cofolding models on a common set of 1,772 cases. With ligand SMILES as input, 22.7–30.8% of top-ranked predictions had a ligand heavy-atom root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) <2 Å after binding-site superposition and a local distance difference test score for protein–ligand interactions (LDDT-PLI) >0.8. Success rates were 10.7–16.5 percentage points lower for complexes released after each model’s training cutoff than for those released earlier. Among post-cutoff cases with evaluable similarity to pre-cutoff benchmark structures, all six models had success rates below 8% in the lowest-similarity group. In paired comparisons of cyclic peptides that could be represented by residue sequences and covalent linkages, Boltz-2 and RoseTTAFold 3 each recovered more experimental binding poses with sequence input than with SMILES. For macrocycles with 30–40 ring atoms, 97.5–100% of each model’s failed top-ranked SMILES predictions had a ligand heavy-atom RMSD of at least 2 Å even after ligand-only superposition. In these cases, the models failed to recover the bound conformation of the ligand itself, limiting their ability to reproduce the experimental binding mode. These findings indicate that current cofolding models have limited ability to generalize to macrocycle binding modes with little structural precedent in the benchmark. Predicted poses for such complexes should be used cautiously in structure-guided macrocycle design.

item.title: CertMat: Formally Certified Robust Phase and Elastic Stability Verification Across One Million Inorganic Crystals
item.description: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) workflows have expanded candidate inorganic crystal catalogs to the million-material scale, yet thermodynamic convex hull stability (Ehull = 0) and mechanical Born stability (C ≻ 0) remain evaluated almost exclusively via floating-point point estimates that neglect energy and stiffness uncertainties. Here we introduce CertMat, an exact rational certificate generator and machine-checked Lean 4 formal verification kernel (leanprover/lean4:v4.16.0, zero Mathlib dependencies, zero sorry or non-standard axioms across 51 mechanized theorems) that certifies worst-case phase and elastic stability over heterogeneous uncertainty boxes. CertMat mechanizes four core theorem families: (1) exact Farkas primal-dual soundness with non-negative margin enforcement (δ ≥ 0) for convex hull decompositions, (2) exact algebraic cancellation of correlated elemental reference-state errors ( ∑ e cieδµe) proving that only uncorrelated residual errors (ηi) can flip phase stability, (3) universal worst-case interval robustness over heterogeneous energy boxes Ei ∈ [Li, Ui] with an exact Charnes–Cooper linear-fractional solver for the critical destabilization radius ε∗(x) and adversarial decomposition Phase Switching, and (4) exact rational LDLT Born positive-definiteness, constructive non-PD strain counterexamples, Voigt Frobenius–Weyl robustness and constructive rank-1 fragility witnesses, and bidirectional pure-rational SO(3)-invariant Mandel/Kelvin Frobenius–Weyl robustness and constructive rank-1 fragility theorems (requiring no irrational √ 2). Auditing 1,044,460 unique crystal phase entries (plus 234,086 matched PBE–r2SCAN sub-hull re-audits, totaling 1,278,545 competed LP audits and 1 uncompeted elemental phase) and 34,323 valid 6 × 6 elastic tensors across Google DeepMind GNoME (PBE and r2SCAN), NIST JARVIS-DFT 3D, and Matbench Discovery WBM—with 95,348 / 95,348 serialized TSV rational certificates machine-verified by the compiled Lean 4 certmat-check binary and an independent pure-Fraction checker (0 failures) plus 540/540 stratified spot-audit dataset-binding checks—we establish four major findings: (i) on 117,043 matched GNoME PBE-vs-r2SCAN crystals, correlated elemental shifts explain R2 = 73.51% of formation-energy discrepancies (reducing MAE from 78.90 to 30.96 meV/atom), and CertMat’s worst-case Fragile classification separates real r2SCAN stability flips with 24.65x relative risk (0.46% vs. 11.36% flip rate, ROC-AUC 0.8948) on exact 117k matched sub-hulls and 5.10x relative risk (96.40% recall) on GNoME’s primary external Decomposition Energy Per Atom column (6.20x relative risk / 97.46% recall on ... MP); (ii) 11,481 of 34,323 (33.45%) valid JARVIS-DFT 3D elastic tensors fail exact Born stability with Lean-certified rational strain witnesses, while 2,643 (11.57%) of Born-PD crystals are fragile under unconstrained 5 GPa Voigt perturbations (Lean-certified via WEYL_FRAGILE) and 1,517 (6.64%) are fragile under SO(3)-invariant 5 GPa Mandel perturbations (bidirectional Lean certification: 22,531 MANDEL_ WEYL_ROBUST + 3,198 MANDEL_WEYL_FRAGILE witnesses); (iii) 19,894 of 42,688 (46.60%) WBM candidates reported stable against the static MP2020 hull collapse to strictly unstable under intra-catalog WBM competition alone (62.19% via same-composition polymorphs, 37.81% via cross-composition decomposition; 40.80% even after unique-prototype deduplication); and (iv) our exact hull audit uncovered a pervasive upstream unit-scaling defect in the published NIST JARVIS-DFT 3D Figshare release (jdft_3d-9-24-2025.json) consistent with dividing per-atom optb88vdw_total_energy a second time by reduced formula-unit atom count Nfu, inflating ehull > 1.0 eV/atom for 63,386 materials (median residual 0.00677 eV vs. 2.605 and 2.108 eV for two negative controls). Code, Lean 4 proofs, and full verification artifacts are publicly available at https://github.com/sunpunggi1/certmat.

item.title: Nonempirical Double-hybrid Functionals Entering the AI Field: the Adaptative LS1DH model
item.description: We introduce a machine-learning-assisted nonempirical double-hybrid density-functional approximation, dubbed adaptative LS1DH or aLS1DH, which combines the theoretical constraints of the linearly scaled one-parameter double-hybrid (LS1DH) model with system-specific flexibility. Based on kernel ridge regression (KRR) and convolutional many-body distribution function (cMBDF) representations, aLS1DH predicts optimal system-dependent fractions of nonlocal exchange and correlation while preserving size consistency. Its performance is assessed on the extended GMTKN55 and on the recently developed CYCLO70. The aLS1DH model consistently improves upon its parent functional, PBE0-DH, rivaling the latest machine-learning-based functionals such as skala functional. These results highlight the potential of machine learning to improve the accuracy of nonempirical double hybrids while retaining their underlying theoretical constraints.

item.title: Tunneling signatures of the Lifshitz transition in a superconducting vortex
item.description: arXiv:2611.31371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states bound to a vortex line in a clean type-II superconductor form one-dimensional minibands that disperse along the vortex. The lowest miniband is separated from the Fermi level by a minigap $E_0\sim\Delta^2/E_F$. A magnetic field shifts the minibands of the two spin projections in opposite directions. At the threshold field $B^*$ the Zeeman energy equals $E_0$. Estimates for FeSe place $B^*$ at a few tesla. The lowest miniband of one spin projection then crosses the Fermi level, and a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea forms inside the vortex core. We develop the theory of tunneling spectra across this Lifshitz transition. We solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically in the quantum limit for all momenta along the vortex and compute the local density of states with thermal and instrumental broadening. The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below $B^*$. It has a maximum near $B^*$ with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity and decreases at higher fields. The next miniband produces a second onset at a finite distance from the center. The zero-bias signal is carried by one spin projection at the center and by the opposite one in the surrounding ring. We then project the screened electron interaction onto the filled miniband. The resulting Luttinger parameter is close to unity, so the core hosts a weakly interacting one-dimensional Fermi gas. Its quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions in analogy with thermalization in quantum wires and at quantum Hall edges. The corresponding relaxation rates are established analytically.

item.title: A fermionic framework for quantum machine learning benchmarks
item.description: arXiv:2611.31458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a framework for building and benchmarking scalable machine learning (ML) models based on simulating free-fermion systems. Our fermionic ML (FermiML) framework is (i) versatile enough to encompass kernel methods and neural networks, (ii) applicable to classification and regression, and (iii) scalable to real-world datasets. FermiML models are quantum circuits sharing the building blocks of most quantum ML (QML) models: (parameterized) qubit rotations and entangling gates. This allows us to build fermionic surrogates that mimic the architecture, and hence the quantum resources and inductive bias, of any QML model while remaining efficiently classically simulable. We thus benchmark QML models against close fermionic counterparts on equal footing and ascertain whether a purported QML gain truly stems from classically inaccessible resources or is an accidental side-effect. Across 31 configurations from five classification datasets, we benchmark quantum kitchen sinks (QKS), instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) and generic parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) models against fermionic surrogates. fQKS significantly outperforms QKS and is statistically indistinguishable from IQP and PQC; fPQC outperforms IQP and QKS and ties PQC in 28 configurations. We also introduce fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression and establish QML baselines for this harder task. Finally, we introduce a fermionic energy-based classifier scalable to large text and image datasets, which outperforms prominent QML models on images, beats or closely trails them on text, and stays close to classical baselines throughout. Our results show that while performance depends sensitively on architecture, FermiML yields fermionic surrogates that challenge or outperform their unrestricted counterparts and fermionic QML models that match the scale of classical baselines on real-world datasets.

item.title: Accelerating Equivariant Interatomic Potentials for Molecular Dynamics through Radial tabulation and Kernel Fusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.31865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) achieve near-quantum-chemical accuracy, but their computational cost and GPU memory footprint restrict molecular dynamics (MD) at extended length and time scales. Even when the tensor product (TP) is accelerated, both bottlenecks remain governed by evaluating and storing per-edge radial weights in the NequIP convolution. We introduce JET-MLIPs (Joint-Kernel Equivariant Convolution with Tabulated Radial Weights for MLIP simulation), a GPU backend applicable to pretrained NequIP-family potentials without retraining. JET-MLIPs replaces the radial multilayer perceptron (MLP) with a piecewise cubic Hermite table and fuses table lookup, spherical harmonics, TP and neighbor aggregation into a single kernel, eliminating per-edge radial-weight and MLP-intermediate storage during force evaluation. Across 15 released potentials from SevenNet, MACE, NequIP-OAM, Nequix and EquFlash on a 5632-atom liquid electrolyte, LAMMPS MD attains 1.5-5.9$\times$ step-time speed-ups and 2.4-24$\times$ peak memory reductions relative to each family's existing TP-accelerated backend on a single H200 GPU while preserving single-precision (fp32) accuracy and dynamical stability. These reductions enable multi-nanosecond transport-property simulations of roughly $10^4$-atom systems on a single GPU and broaden access to large-scale equivariant MLIP MD on widely available GPUs.

item.title: From Weighted Frontier d-States to Geometric Descriptors for Atomically Dispersed Catalysts at the Molecule-Solid Crossover
item.description: arXiv:2611.32059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomically dispersed catalysts exhibit molecule-solid crossover character when localized metal orbitals hybridize with support-derived bands, a regime not fully captured by either a d-band-center description or a frontier-orbital picture. We establish an electronic-to-geometric framework for oxygen reduction across fourteen metals. N-to-P substitution in M-N4 sites raises theoretical onset potentials in 13 systems, with Rh-N3P reaching 0.88 V, comparable to the Pt(111) benchmark. Scaling relations reduce *OOH, *O, and *OH thermodynamics to $\Delta$G*OH. M-N4 follows a dyz-dominated frontier-orbital picture, whereas M-N3P requires a weighted frontier d-state representation built from adsorption-relevant orbitals and their occupancies. The resulting $\epsilon$WFDS correlates with $\Delta$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.92, compared with 0.83 for the d-band center and 0.64 for the frontier-orbital. The identified roles of orbital occupancy and local coordination suggest an interpretable geometric descriptor, $\zeta$M-N3P = nd/rM-P, that predicts $\Delta$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.96. The ORR volcano analysis identifies strong-binding systems and motivates axial oxygen coordination. This design raises onset potentials by 0.70-2.46 V, and the M-N3PO descriptor predicts $\Delta$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.91. By bridging frontier-orbital and d-band-center descriptions, the framework provides a physically grounded electronic representation and a geometry-based screening route compatible with machine-learned interatomic potentials.

item.title: Reconfigurable Chiral Phonons and Their Selection in Asymmetrically Stacked Graphene MoirMoir\'{e} Superlattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.32466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral phonons, lattice vibrations carrying angular momentum, offer a new handle for controlling phonon-mediated phenomena in condensed matter, yet their on-demand generation and deterministic control remain challenging. Here we show, using helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy, that asymmetrically stacked graphene moir\'{e} superlattices provide a reconfigurable platform for chiral phonons. We observe a finite degree of circular polarization for both chiral interlayer shear phonons and intralayer optical phonons. A chiral-phonon Raman-tensor model attributes this response to interfacial $C_{2}$-symmetry breaking together with Raman resonance within the van Hove singularity region. Reversing either the twist sense or the stacking order inverts the degree of circular polarization through the spatial transformations linking the corresponding stacking geometries. By tuning the excitation energy and twist angle, we achieve nearly full-range control of the degree of circular polarization of interlayer shear phonons, from $-1$ to $1$, while gate-induced interlayer potential redistribution enables substantial and reversible in situ modulation. These results establish asymmetrically stacked graphene moir\'{e} superlattices as a versatile platform for generating and controlling chiral phonons, with implications for optoelectronic and quantum technologies.

item.title: Thermodynamics of complex crystals from a generalized mean-field bond model
item.description: arXiv:2611.32609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend our previously introduced mean-field bond model from unary fcc lattices to crystals with multiple chemical species and sublattices, accurately predicting finite-temperature thermodynamics without statistical sampling. Our generalization reformulates the model in terms of the Wyckoff positions of the crystal, representing each by one atom, and solving for the bond density of the reference bond of each of its neighbor shells. Bond-bond correlation functions are built from the zero-temperature force constants, allowing the deviation of every bond in the crystal to be expressed through linear functions of the reference bond of a shell. Thermodynamic self-consistency is enforced by requiring a single virial temperature for the whole crystal, and compatibility of average bond lengths with crystal volume. Model predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations of unary, binary, and ternary crystals using Morse-type bonding potentials, parametrized for each shell from the force constants of empirical interatomic potentials at several isotropic strains. In each case, the predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with the simulations to within their statistical uncertainty. We discuss strategies for combining the model with bonding potentials parametrized from first principles and foundation models to predict the finite-temperature thermodynamics of complex crystals at ab initio accuracy without statistical sampling.

item.title: Neutron Spectroscopy Transformed: Deuterated ZIF-8 and Machine-Learned Potentials Catch Nitrogen Threading Its Gates
item.description: arXiv:2611.32739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a step change in what inelastic neutron scattering (INS) can reveal, by combining machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with deliberate deuteration of the sample. INS's prowess in charting framework and guest motions within porous materials during in situ dosing has historically had one caveat: costly density-functional-theory calculations are a major bottleneck in the speed and depth of analysis. We show that rapid frontier MLIPs remove this bottleneck on both counts, keeping pace with the experiment while bringing a new level of insight. Deuterating the linkers of ZIF-8 pries apart bands that overlap in the hydrogenous framework, and we test four MLIPs against eight stages of nitrogen dosing at 77 K. On loading, a previously unobserved band appears at 270 cm^-1 and grows gradually through the dosing series. The simulations trace it to single N2 molecules threaded end-on through four-ring windows, each turning its ring of linkers and propping the window open, and unbiased dynamics catch molecules threading into the windows on their own, finding a free-energy trap that crowding stabilizes. This is the first vibrational signature of the threaded state and, crucially, its intensity directly counts the threading over the slow, macroscopic timescale of gas uptake, in situ. More broadly, the simulations explain how each framework band responds to its guests, establishing MLIP-assisted inelastic neutron scattering as a route to mechanism, not just assignment.

item.title: Anharmonic enhancement of thermal conductivity in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$: A consistent picture from molecular dynamics and Wigner transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.33089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anharmonicity limits heat conduction in crystals, but its role in amorphous solids, where heat is carried mainly by tunneling between quasi-degenerate vibrations, remains unsettled. Here we disentangle the contributions of structural disorder, quantum statistics, and anharmonicity to the thermal conductivity of amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ (aGST), the prototypical phase-change memory material. Using a single machine-learned potential trained on first-principles data, we compare classical equilibrium and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (MD), which include anharmonicity to all orders, with harmonic Allen-Feldman theory and the anharmonic Wigner transport equation, both of which include quantum statistics. Four MD approaches agree on a conductivity of 0.171-0.181 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, about 16% above the harmonic Allen-Feldman value for the same model, and the Wigner formulation bridges the two: with classical statistics, it agrees with MD to within 5%. We trace this anharmonic enhancement to vibrational couplings that grow with the frequency difference between modes, so that anharmonic broadening opens additional channels for heat conduction. A comparison with silica, alumina, and disordered carbons reveals three regimes, in which anharmonicity reduces, barely affects, or enhances the conductivity. The predicted glass-like increase of the conductivity with temperature is consistent with thermoreflectance measurements. These results show that anharmonicity has no universal effect in disordered solids, and can promote rather than limit heat transport in strongly disordered materials.

item.title: Antiferromagnetic phase of MnTe2: spin-order-induced renormalization of phonon Raman spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2611.33156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, two modes of spin wave excitations (magnons) were detected in Raman scattering spectra of MnTe2. It is an unconventional magnet that features a pyrite-type crystal structure hosting a non-collinear, non-coplanar antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin order below the N\'eel temperature. In this brief communication, the focus is primarily on the effect of spin ordering on lattice dynamics (phonons) that has been established through temperature (5 - 300 K), linear polarization angle (0 deg - 360 deg) and external magnetic field (up to 16 T) dependent measurements. It has been found that below the magnetic transition temperature, the frequencies of four out of five Raman-active lattice vibrations (i.e., Eg and three Tg phonon modes) revealed significant departure from the mechanism of the three-phonon anharmonic decay described by Klemens model. Here, we propose a new model considering spin-phonon coupling to explain frequency renormalization of the phonon part of the Raman spectrum upon the para-/antiferro- (PM/AFM) magnetic phase transition change in MnTe2. Through employing Green's function formalism, we show that a simple two-sublattice collinear antiferromagnet approach follows well both spin ordering induced hardening and softening of phonon modes observed in AFM phase of MnTe2 upon cooling. Additionally, the detailed temperature and field dependences of the energy for both magnon modes are presented. In addition to unexpected twofold anisotropy of the higher energy magnon mode (approx. 3.5 meV) unveiled in crossed configuration, our magneto-optical measurements revealed a subtle, yet definite softening trend for the lower energy mode (approx. 2.6 meV). Although the precise reasons for these effects remain unclear, we put forward a symmetry reduction in the local atomic surroundings as a possible mechanism for discussion.

item.title: Systematic and accurate anharmonic formation free energies of metastable defects via a constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force framework
item.description: arXiv:2608.20902v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computing the formation free energies of metastable defects at finite temperature remains challenging due to anharmonicity, the multiplicity of basins and the frequent occurrence of migration events. Using the previously introduced constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force method (BABFc), we establish a practical thermodynamic integration framework for computing restricted anharmonic formation free energies associated with individual metastable defect basins. We demonstrate that BABFc can be exploited as a robust, systematic and numerically efficient tool for addressing a long standing bottleneck in atomistic materials science: the finite temperature thermodynamic characterization of metastable defects in complex, highly anharmonic energy landscapes. The proposed workflow requires only a reference local minimum and a confinement strategy and does not rely on defect specific collective variables. It therefore provides a general route to assign well-defined free energies to individual metastable basins, even when these basins are separated by low barriers and embedded in a dense landscape of competing configurations. In this setting, BABFc enables stable, bias corrected free energy estimates with statistical accuracies at the meV/atom level and a very low failure rate, including for systems containing approximately one thousand atoms. We demonstrate this capability through thousands of independent free energy calculations covering hundreds of four-interstitial and four-vacancy configurations in bcc $\alpha$-Fe over a broad temperature range, using both a traditional empirical potential and a data driven force field.

item.title: Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson simulation of the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model
item.description: arXiv:2611.32895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard (JCH) model describes the interaction of light and matter in coupled optical cavities and provides a framework for studying their quantum dynamics. In this work, we design a Trotterized quantum circuit to investigate the real-time dynamics of the JCH model using Bosonic Qiskit and a Matrix Product State (MPS) backend. We simulate single-polariton transport and benchmark site occupations against exact diagonalization results. We then extend the simulations to the two-excitation sector under a hard-core photon constraint, examining excitation transport and symmetry properties. Finally, we study the dependence of bipartite entanglement entropy on the inter-cavity photon-hopping strength. The results illustrate how hybrid qubit-boson circuits, simulated with matrix product states, can be used to study light-matter lattice dynamics. This work provides a numerical benchmark for extending hybrid simulation approaches to more complex interacting and open light-matter systems.

item.title: Nanoindentation induced plasticity in equiatomic MoTaW alloys by experimentally guided machine learning molecular dynamics simulations
item.description: arXiv:2601.06846v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCA) exhibit exceptional strength and thermal stability, yet their plastic deformation mechanisms under complex contact loading remain insufficiently understood. Here, the nanoindentation response of an equiatomic MoTaW alloy is investigated through a combined experimental and atomistically resolved modeling approach. Spherical nanoindentation experiments are coupled with large scale molecular dynamics simulations employing a tabulated low dimensional Gaussian Approximation Potential (tabGAP), enabling near DFT accuracy. A physics based similarity criterion, implemented via PCA of load-displacement curves, is used to identify mechanically representative experimental responses for quantitative comparison with simulations. Indentation stress-strain curves are constructed yielding excellent agreement in the elastic regime between experiment and simulation, with reduced Young's moduli of approximately 270 GPa. Generalized stacking fault energy calculations reveal elevated unstable stacking- and twinning-fault energies in MoTaW relative to pure refractory elements, indicating suppressed localized shear and a preference for dislocation-mediated plasticity. Atomistic analyses demonstrate a strong crystallographic dependence of plastic deformation, with symmetric {110}<111> slip activation and four-fold rosette pile-ups for the [001] orientation, and anisotropic slip, strain localization, and enhanced junction formation for [011]. Local entropy and polyhedral template matching analyses further elucidate dislocation network evolution and deformation-induced local structural transformations. Overall, this study establishes a direct mechanistic link between fault energetics, orientation-dependent dislocation activity, and experimentally observed nanoindentation behavior in RCCA.

item.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
item.description: arXiv:2601.15735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. In the MAGNDATA database, 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. With the $k$ index fixed to its experimental value, about nine structures are generated per material on average. We perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. The characteristic energy scale among oriented SSA structures is only approximately 0.29 meV per magnetic atom, about 300 times smaller than that of distinct SSA structures. These results demonstrate that oriented SSG-based enumeration, combined with the two-step calculations for SSA and oriented SSA structures, provides an efficient and robust route for large-scale magnetic-structure prediction.

item.title: AutoXRD: Autonomous Large Language Model Agents and Comprehensive Evaluation for Powder X-Ray Diffraction Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2609.00070v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) is a foundational technique for structural and phase characterization in materials science, yet automating its analysis and evaluating it end-to-end remains challenging. Doing so requires an agent to interpret diffraction patterns, run refinement software, manage strongly coupled parameters in a physically meaningful order, and assess both numerical fit quality and physical validity. We propose AutoXRD, an LLM agent framework that organizes powder XRD analysis into refinement stages, uses diffraction diagnostics to select actions, and checks the resulting fits against crystallographic and physical criteria. We further introduce XRDBench with two complementary tracks. XRDBench-QA contains 100 tasks assessing scientific reasoning and decision-making, whereas XRDBench-E2E contains 34 end-to-end workflows requiring data interpretation, crystallographic software execution, iterative refinement, evidence preservation, and reporting. Across 1,340 runs of ten recent LLMs, models average only 57.8 out of 100, falling from 61.9 on XRDBench-QA to 53.7 on XRDBench-E2E. At the task level, they perform best on refinement-history assessment and result acceptance, but remain substantially weaker on refinement-action selection, phase quantification, indexing, and Rietveld refinement. Among individual models, GPT-5.6 Sol achieves the highest overall score of 81.1, GPT-5.6 Terra scores highest on XRDBench-E2E (81.0), and GPT-5.6 Luna provides the best score-cost trade-off. Moreover, ablations confirm that all six AutoXRD components consistently improve performance. Finally, execution-trace analysis reveals recurring failures in coupled-parameter control, quantitative reasoning, evidence preservation, and workflow termination, motivating stronger scientific constraints, uncertainty quantification, and more efficient planning.

item.title: ZStar: A unified toolkit for polarization, Born effective charges, dielectric and piezoelectric responses, and infrared and Raman spectra
item.description: arXiv:2609.16802v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Polarization and the response to atomic displacements determine the dielectric, piezoelectric, and vibrational spectroscopy of materials, yet these quantities are usually obtained through separate workflows within ABACUS. Here, we present ZStar, an open-source Python toolkit that unifies these calculations. Using ABACUS and PYATB, ZStar derives Born effective charges (BECs) and zone-center force constants from one symmetry-adapted displacement set, and reuses the displaced electronic matrices for Raman spectra. Berry phases in periodic directions combined with charge-density dipoles in nonperiodic directions extend the method from bulk crystals (3D) to 2D and 1D materials and molecules (0D). These BECs and phonon modes give infrared intensities and the lattice contribution to the dielectric response. From finite strains, ZStar further obtains clamped-ion and relaxed-ion piezoelectric coefficients. This unified workflow reduces the computational cost by up to 4.2$\times$ for BECs and zone-center phonons and 8.4$\times$ for combined infrared and Raman calculations. ZStar also supports machine-learned models by generating training data and post-processing prediction results into physical properties.

item.title: Atom as an Agent: Emergent Order by Collective Predictive Coding
item.description: arXiv:2610.36673v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: What is the intrinsic reason of emergence of macroscopic order parameter out of microscopic systems? In this article, we apply to physics the collective predictive coding (CPC), the theory of language/symbol emergence. As our language emerges out of our human communications, physical macroscopic order parameter emerges out of communications among atoms --- each atom is regarded as an agent who predicts each other's behavior through inference. We present three examples of classical spin systems: two-dimensional ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, a two-dimensional spin model with competing stripe orders, and the fully connected Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model. In all of these examples, proper macroscopic order parameters including the replica overlap emerge automatically through communication informatics of CPC, only from observed spin configurations. We call the learned macroscopic coordinate the collective predictive order. Furthermore, for the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, the equilibrium distribution of the collective predictive order yields an emergent potential with the symmetry and thermal evolution characteristic of a Landau potential. Notably, the emergence of the collective predictive order does not refer to any structure of microscopic Hamiltonians/Lagrangians. Thus our ``Atom-as-an-Agent" (AaaA) principle offers a completely data-driven method for the emergence of macroscopic order, that is, machine learning physics.

item.title: From sketch to publication-ready flowchart: how AI tools can bridge the gap

The use of generative AI is a practical way to translate hand-drawn scientific diagrams into digital formats without handing over total control, explains Ensar Aydemir.

item.title: A training-free semantic cognition framework unlocks interpretable, actionable management for battery energy storage systems
item.description: Yang et al. introduce TimeSeries2Report, a framework for translating lithium-ion battery time series into structured, human-readable reports. Validated on laboratory cells and real-world storage data, these reports help large language models interpret battery behavior and support state estimation, anomaly detection, and charging/discharging decisions without task-specific retraining.

item.title: Learning when to use physical relationships in descriptor-based tabular machine learning
item.description: Multiple properties of materials and energy devices are linked by known physical relationships, yet descriptor-based machine-learning models commonly predict each property independently, here termed Direct prediction. This study tests whether these relationships remain useful when their inputs are themselves model predictions. Across 16 target–route endpoints spanning solid-state ionic conductors, thermoelectric materials, liquid metal batteries and photovoltaic devices, reconstruction through predicted auxiliary quantities and known physical relationships, termed Physics-only, was less accurate than Direct for 13 endpoints, showing that predicted inputs can turn physically valid relationships into error-amplifying transformations. A residual model correcting the Physics-only estimate, termed Residual-only, recovered much of this systematic distortion but was not consistently superior to Direct and often exhibited similar sample-wise errors. PhysicsGate therefore retains Direct as an anchor and learns a bounded, sample-specific interpolation towards Residual-only using training-side out-of-fold reliability signals. At the domain level, PhysicsGate gave the largest mean paired gain of the six compared architectures in all four domains, equivalent to root-mean-square error reductions of 12.9% for liquid metal batteries, 8.9% for thermoelectric materials (2.8% with the thermoelectric Direct model at the source authors’ settings), 5.2% for solid-state ionic conductors and 0.4% for photovoltaic devices; the liquid metal battery interval included zero. PhysicsGate also ranked first for 15 of the 16 endpoints, which are not independent because routes within a dataset share records. Repeated-split analyses showed that sample adaptation outperformed training-selected fixed blending for thermoelectric but not for photovoltaic targets. Performance differences were associated with auxiliary-error propagation, residual correctability, branch-error redundancy and learnable variation in branch utility. Each of these quantities can be estimated from training-side out-of-fold predictions before evaluation on held-out data.

item.title: A novel ensemble machine learning framework considering dynamic error reciprocal weighting for state of health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
item.description:
Publication date: 2 February 2027

Source: Journal of Energy Storage, Volume 184

Author(s): Yuxuan Wang, Hehua Su, Shenhua Zhong, Yaojie Shi, Xiaoqing Zhu, Xing Ju, Chao Xu

item.title: Ligand Connectivity Control of Hubbard Interactions at Metal Sites in Frameworks and Oxides Revealed by Theory-Guided Agents
item.description: Coordination chemistry ranks ligands via the spectrochemical and nephelauxetic series, but both rely on d-d spectra and leave d⁰ metals unranked. Ligands should similarly govern the Hubbard U (on-site Coulomb repulsion) and intersite V (metal-ligand repulsion), which single-U-per-element DFT+U obscures. Here two LLM agents, a Teacher asking from theory and a Student answering from data, propose ligand rules from linear-response data on 241 metal-organic frameworks and 57 oxides, which we establish from response matrices and first-principles calculations. At fixed element, oxidation state and coordination number, the first coordination sphere sets the U of Zr and Hf via metal d–carboxylate O 2p coupling, and V ranks oxygen donors by protonation and bridging mode as a ligand series for d⁰ metals. In iron oxoanion salts, the oxoanion central atom raises Fe U through the same coupling, so a metal site is defined by its donors and each donor by what else it is bonded to. This ligand connectivity explains how capping ligands set the electronic sites of defective frameworks. Tabulated by ligand type, U and V replace linear-response calculations costing about 400 times the ground state and reproduce the DFT+U+V electronic structure of a Zr node within a few meV. Controlled experiments show that theory-guided questions move agents from statistical association to falsifiable mechanistic hypotheses. This work supports high-throughput modelling of charge localization and transfer, rational ligand engineering and physical-chemistry discovery from existing data.

item.title: Checking the checks on quantum-chemical outputs: four open-source tools for stationary points, reaction paths, spectra and slab convergence, tested against independent references
item.description: The numbers that leave a quantum-chemical calculation are usually processed by short scripts that are rarely tested (stationary points, free energies, tunnelling factors, spectra, surface energies). We tested four open-source Python packages that automate such steps, QMCert, NEBCert, SpecCert and CatCert, against independent references: the cclib parser, GoodVibes and the program’s own output (59 ORCA 6.1 calculations); ORCA’s fullprecision files, overreact and a 40-digit reference (12 ORCA nudged-elasticband runs and 720 tunnelling cases); ORCA’s spectrum tool, the NIST CCCBDB scaling-factor table and pymatgen (8 molecules and 9 VASP calculations); and ASE and hand calculations (an Al(111) slab series and H adsorption, Quantum ESPRESSO). The corrected releases reproduce every reference to its printing precision. The tests exposed defects in the first releases that no author-written unit test had caught: a quasi-harmonic correction that invited users to apply it twice (up to 0.73 kcal mol−1), Eckart tunnelling factors wrong by up to 10⁴⁶, a failed job passed as a 71,706 kcal mol−1 barrier, absorption coefficients 24% too low, invented infrared intensities, d-band centres off by up to 0.77 eV, and a surface-energy convergence rule whose verdict depends on where the thickness series stops (PASS at 7 layers, FAIL at 11, on the same calculations). Two optimisations of open-shell molecules converged, with every criterion met, to saddle points. The shared lesson: a check must be tested on real outputs, designed failures and an independent implementation, and its verdict reported with what it did not test.

item.title: Harmonic descriptor for enhanced four-phonon scattering based on local phonon-state accumulation and energy matching
item.description:
Author(s): Yuan Yao, Hao Chen, Chang-Hao Ding, Wen-Wen Liu, Yu-Jia Zeng, Nannan Luo, Jiang Zeng, Li-Ming Tang, and Ke-Qiu Chen

Four-phonon (4ph) scattering has emerged as an important source of intrinsic phonon resistance in strongly anharmonic crystals. Interpretable harmonic spectral indicators could help prioritize materials for explicit higher-order transport calculations. In this work, we systematically investigate 4ph…

item.title: Digitising Polyoxometalate Syntheses
item.description: Polyoxometalates (POMs) are structurally diverse metal-oxo clusters whose syntheses are governed by a delicate interplay of parameters, including pH, counter-cations, and concentration. To convert this synthetic knowledge into a machine-readable format, we devised a 4-stage automated pipeline. The pipeline employs a series of Large Language Model (LLM) agents for text pre-processing, reagent extraction, and procedure structuring, followed by a final data assembly module to consolidate the outputs. This workflow transformed 405 unstructured synthesis descriptions into a strict JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) corpus containing structured metadata, reagents, and operational steps. The resulting database is ready for rapid querying and data-driven optimisation of new POM materials.

item.title: From Bench to Game Engine: An Instructor-Built Suite of 3D Laboratory Simulations Created with Generative AI
item.description: Virtual chemistry laboratories have historically required either a commercial subscription or a software development team, placing custom simulations out of reach for most instructors. I report the design and construction of a suite of browser-playable 3D laboratory simulations for a non-science-majors chemistry course that has no formal laboratory component — density of an unknown metal, pH of common solutions, double replacement reactions, separations by paper chromatography, and physical and chemical changes — that I built alone in the Unity game engine, with no prior game-development experience, using a large-language-model coding assistant connected directly to the engine. Each lab pairs a 3D fume hood, rendered by a Unity WebGL build, with an HTML worksheet that checks readings, assigns per-student unknowns, and prints a one-page report; the answer data lives in the compiled build rather than in the page, so students cannot read it from the source. The labs serve two purposes: laboratory experience for students who would otherwise have none, and continuity of instruction when hurricane closures disrupt the weekly schedule. I describe the development workflow, the division of labor between instructor and AI, the design decisions that keep the simulations chemically honest, the time and cost involved, and the limitations encountered. All builds, worksheet pages, and prelab reviews are freely available on GitHub. The approach offers a reproducible path for instructors to author their own laboratory simulations: the five described here were built in about one month.

item.title: Surfactant-Toolkit and SurfBench-200: an open computation toolkit and a benchmark of tool-augmented language-model reasoning in surfactant science
item.description: Language models are increasingly used as research assistants in chemistry, but their quantitative work insurfactantscience hasnotbeen measured.We introduce Surfactant-Toolkit, an MIT-licensed Python library and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server with 123 validated tools for micellization, mixed micelles, adsorption, emulsions, micelle structure and transport,andSurfBench-200,200graduate-levelquestionswhosereferenceanswersare computed by the toolkit and graded field by field by deterministic scripts. Without tools, five frontier models passed 52.5% to 66.0% of the questions; with the toolkit, the four models run in both conditions passed 92.0% to 98.5% (exact McNemar p < 0.0001 for each), and the open-weightDeepSeek (92.0%) outscored every modelwithouttools.Remaining failures shifted from wrong magnitudes tochoices ofmodelorconvention:toolslargely remove calculation errors, not errors of judgement. Asked the same questions again, every model changed some answers and at least once stated something the data did not support. Used for new findings, the toolkit and two augmented models produced five results on seven research problems that we could not find in the literature. Used for error finding, it showed that five recent papers each contain a value or conclusion that does not follow from their own printed data, from a reversed interaction-parameter sign to a physically impossible molecular area; two frontier models given the same values recomputed nearly all of these without tools but called an undetermined result contradicted. All questions, transcripts, graders and code are released, with SurfactantKit-Studio, a local application for researchers. 1.
